html:
Ignaz Semmelweis was a doctor, born in 1818 in Buda, who in 1847 at the Vienna General Hospital showed that doctors' unwashed hands were spreading deadly childbed fever among new mothers.

In one maternity clinic run by doctors and students, who came straight from dissecting corpses, far more mothers died than in another run by midwives. Semmelweis had the doctors wash their hands in chlorinated lime, and deaths fell sharply. Many doctors rejected his idea, which came before germ theory, and he grew bitter. He returned to Pest and wrote a book on it in 1861. In 1865 he was taken to an asylum in Vienna, where he died two weeks later after a beating by guards. Pasteur and Lister later proved him right. He is called the saviour of mothers.
sum: Ignaz Semmelweis was a doctor, born in 1818 in Buda, who in 1847 at the Vienna General Hospital showed that doctors' unwashed hands were spreading deadly childbed fever among new mothers.
